ActiveSession.description: **The session record, in `identity.session`** (3 October 2026, CHG-R1S-008; the HLD/LLD cross-check and the r1 gate). Until then it was "none — Redis session registry", and 11 operations wrote a session no SQL created: nothing defined its columns, so `listActiveSessions` could not page, filter by workstation or venue, or run under row-level security. The row is the record of record, tenant-scoped and under RLS like every identity table; Redis stays the token cache in front of it (ADR-0004: a session is a token with a validity window, and the cache answers that check). The names and `hasOpenShift` are read with it, not stored.

status.description: **A registry that only holds live sessions cannot answer why one ended.** Kept on the record so a supervisor asking *what happened to till 4* gets `terminated` or `expired` rather than an absence.

sessionId.description: **The session's `identity.session.id`, written as text, and the key `forceLogout` takes in its path** (R8 blocker fix, IDENTITY-C02). A client lists sessions, picks one and passes this value as `sessionId`; nothing else names a session on the wire. The server opens a session with `session_id` set to its `id` as text, so the stored `session_id` (the token's `sid`) and the id are one value and a lookup by either finds the row. It stays `type: string` here so a client built at r1 still validates; it is always a uuid, as `Session.sessionId` declares.

endedAt.description: When the session ended; null exactly while `active`, and set on every other status (R8 blocker IDENTITY-C46, CHG-R8MIG-015; a table CHECK since ADAM CR-242, 26 October 2026).

endedByPrincipalId.description: Who ended it (`forceLogout`'s caller or supervisor; the principal itself when `changeOwnCredential` ended its other sessions); null when the principal signed out or it expired.

endReason.description: Why it was ended, as `forceLogout` was given it (or `supervisor-takeover` from the till door, or `credential-changed` when `changeOwnCredential` ended it; ADAM CR-242).

workstationName.description: Read from the workstation with the row.

hasOpenShift.description: Revoking this session leaves cash unreconciled. **Computed on read, from Identity's own projection** (decided 20 October 2026, Chinmay, R8 blocker cause IDENTITY-C51, option A; CHG-R8SPN-036): true when `identity.open_shift_marker` (`OpenShiftMarker`) holds a row for this principal at this session's workstation. Identity is Foundation and never reads `orders.pos_shift` (ADR-0028), so the marker is fed by Shift's events, as `identity.subject_holding` is fed by Orders'. BO-053 and POS-000 read it here; never stored on the session.

AiApprovalRequestScore.description: **Context for an approval reviewer** (11.1.73..75): risk, priority and a suggested escalation for one pending request, the latest per request. **There is no approve or reject field, by design** (minutes of 8 September: AI in approvals never recommends or influences approve or reject).

riskBand.description: Design 5.6: a risk score and band, never a probability.

priorityScore.description: For ordering work in an inbox; higher first.

escalationSuggestion.description: A suggestion for an SLA problem, carried out if at all by a person or the tenant's SLA policy.

scopePath.description: **The partition key** (ADR-0005). Row-level security compares it with `ticvai.scope_paths` (`platform.apply_scope_rls`), on the tenant database and on the AI log database alike (design 3.1).

deliveryChannels.description: How it reaches people (29 September, build, 18.1.5). `inApp` always; `push` to the targeted people's registered staff phones (tenancy `RegisteredDevice`, kind `mobileHandset`). `emergency` is sent by both whatever is set here.

AnnouncementKind.description: `emergency` is not a louder `operational`. It overrides the home screen, bypasses quiet hours, requires acknowledgement, and carries a separate permission.

outstanding.description: **The list that matters.** For an operational notice it measures whether anyone read it; during an emergency it is the roll call.

id.description: **Added 20 August.** The schema reference derives table columns from API response schemas, and a response is not a table — this one returned everything a caller needs and not the row's own identity, so the table had no key and no row could be addressed, updated or deleted. Found by an audit of all 365 tables, not by a reader.

principalId.description: The approver; null when an external workflow system decided (`externalApproverRef` set).

externalApproverRef.description: Who decided in the external provider's system, as it named them (`recordExternalApprovalDecision`); null for an internal approver (CHG-R8MIG-009).

externalApproverName.description: The external approver's display name, where the provider sent one (CHG-R8MIG-009).

decision.description: `return` and `requestInformation` are stored as decisions too, their comment in `comment` (`decideApprovalRequest`; CHG-R8MIG-009).

delegatorPrincipalId.description: A principal id (`identity.Principal.id`). This contract stores the id only; the name to show, and the people to pick from, come from `identity.listPrincipals` and `identity.getPrincipal`.

delegatePrincipalId.description: A principal id, resolved to a name the same way as `delegatorPrincipalId`.

kinds.description: Absent means everything the delegator may approve.

maxAmount.description: A delegate may be given less authority than the delegator, never more.

to.description: **Required.** An open-ended delegation is an approver who quietly stopped approving and a delegate who does not know they still hold it.

scopePath.description:
**The partition key** (ADR-0005). Added 31 August: the operations that write this table declare a scope and the table carried no column for it — **49 tables were in that state**, so a row could be written at venue scope and then read by anything that could reach the table.

**`scope_path` rather than a specific id** because it is prefix-comparable: `uae.dubai` contains `uae.dubai.marina`, and one index answers every level of the walk.

**Operations write it at `venue` scope.**

delegationType.description: The composite screen's `delegationType` (planned absence, temporary cover ...), for display and reporting; the engine treats every delegation alike (4 October 2026, CHG-FXC-005).

maxPercentage.description: A percentage cap beside `maxAmount` (the composite's `authorityPercentage`, CHG-FXC-005).

requiredRoleId.description: A role the delegate must hold for the delegation to act (the composite's `requiredRole`); checked when the delegate decides, refused with 409 at creation where the delegate does not hold it (CHG-FXC-005).

ApprovalKind.description:
11.1.7 and 11.1.30–11.1.37. **The first four already exist as bespoke implementations** and this contract is what they collapse into.
**Which actions route here — decided 28 September, audit R144.** Finance and procurement acts go through this engine to a **finance approver**: closing a fiscal period (`periodClose`), reopening one (`periodReopen`), cancelling a purchase order (`purchaseOrderCancel`) and closing one short (`purchaseOrderShortClose`). The tenant default matrix for each of these names the finance approver role; a venue may tighten it and never loosen it. Starting a release rollout routes through `releasePromotion` to the platform release manager (a holder of `PLATFORM_RELEASE_PROMOTE`). **Not every `requiresApproval` goes here:** reopening a shift, recounting a stock count and a retail return above the venue threshold take a supervisor's step-up on the same device instead, and never raise a request.
**Catalogue change requests route through `productChange` and `pricingChange`** (decided 29 September, writers pass): a product change and a price or pricing change raised in `catalogue` ask for approval under these two kinds, so a venue can route product edits and price edits to different approvers.

**Optional review steps a venue switches on, decided 2 October 2026** (Chinmay; CHG-CSP-036, CHG-CSP-028, CHG-CSP-031). Each is an existing kind narrowed by the rule's `subjectTypes`, so no kind is added (a new value here would be a breaking change against r1) and each is off until the venue saves an active matrix for it:
- **A platform suspension or reactivation of a tenant** (`configurationChange`, subject `tenant`, `subjectContract` `subscription`; ADAM CR-172; lead''s ruling on lane H review 3 N-1, 20 October 2026; CHG-R8SPN-015): decided by the platform, never by the tenant''s own approvers. It is routed only by the **platform rule**, held in the control plane and seeded when the platform is provisioned, whose approvers hold `PLATFORM_TENANT_MANAGE`, with four eyes (the operator who raised it cannot decide it). It is not off by default like the review steps below: the platform rule always exists, and without it `createApprovalRequest` refuses `422 no-approval-route`.
- **A purchase order** (`requisition`, subject `purchaseOrder`; Chinmay, 3 October 2026, Block A business rules; CHG-RUL-004): the PO approval matrix. Blanket and RFQ-award orders are raised without a requisition and are approved here instead; `inventory.createPurchaseOrder` asks for every order, by kind and value. - **Publishing white-label content** (`configurationChange`, subject `whiteLabelPublication`): simulate, then a single publish by a holder of the permission; a review step only where the venue sets one up (batch 1, CMS-014; DEC-156). - **Recording F&B waste above a value** (`stockWriteOff`, subject `fnbWaste`): the venue's waste-approval policy, value bands as `minAmount` and `maxAmount`, photo evidence above a value held by fnb (batch 6 #192, BO-139; DEC-192; R144). - **Publishing an access topology** (`configurationChange`, subject `topologyPublication`): second-person approval when the venue switches it on (batch 6 #230, BO-153; DEC-230). - **A permanent identity lock, a whitelist entry, or releasing a full-identity or permanent lock** (`accessPermissionChange`, subjects `identityLock`, `whitelistEntry`, `identityLockRelease`): always a second approver, never for an until-end-of-day lock (critical set 1, BO-229 and BO-247; DEC-254, DEC-260); the tenant default matrix names the security approver role and a venue may tighten it, never remove it.

**A sales channel going live** (ADAM CR-211, option A, decided 25 October 2026; CHG-R10CAT-003).
`configurationChange`, subject `salesChannel`, `subjectContract` `catalogue`, `subjectId` the channel: raised by
catalogue `publishChannelReadinessValidation` on `submitForApproval`, and named by its `scheduleActivation` and
`activate`, which are refused until it is approved. An existing kind narrowed by `subjectTypes`, so no kind is
added.

**A rota shift swap** (4 October 2026, CHG-FXC-008; Sprint 1-2 judging: `workforce.requestShiftSwap` raised a request
with no kind that fits). `configurationChange`, subject `shiftSwap`, `subjectContract` `workforce`, `subjectId` the
ShiftSwap id: an existing kind narrowed by `subjectTypes`, as the optional review steps above, so no kind is added.

**A guest's privacy request** (ADAM CR-101, accepted 15 October 2026; CHG-R10ID-016). `configurationChange`,
`subjectContract` `identity`, `subjectId` the guest's subject id, subject `subjectDataExport` for
`exportSubjectData` and `subjectErasure` for `deleteGuestAccount`: an existing kind narrowed by `subjectTypes`,
so no kind is added. Raised by Identity in process for the guest, it records the guest as `requestedBySubjectId`
(`requestedByPrincipalId` null). A guest's own request needs no human approval step (ADR-0047 section 7); a
tenant that wants one saves a rule for these subject types.

ApprovalMatrix.description: **Which matrix routes a request, and which version of it** (ADAM CR-102, option 1, accepted 15 October 2026; CHG-R10ID-015). Matrices resolve up the scope tree as configuration does (ADR-0018: nearest ancestor wins): for the request's `kind` at its `scopePath`, the matrix of the nearest node, the venue's, else the region's, else the tenant's, routes it alone; its rules are not followed by an ancestor's, because a venue or region matrix may only tighten what it inherits (`loosensParentRule`), so the nearest matrix already holds the ancestor's floor. At a node, the matrix **in force** is its highest `version`; when that version has `isActive` false, the node sets no matrix of that kind and the next ancestor's applies (confirmed by the lead, 25 October 2026, r10 round 3; CHG-R10ID-020). The request stores the matrix it was routed by (`approvalMatrixId`) and its `matrixVersion`, so a decision is checked against exactly that rule set.

version.description:
11.1.80. **A request is decided by the rules it was raised under.** Changing the matrix mid-flight would mean an approver answering a question that changed while they read it.
**(`kind`, `scopePath`, `version`) is unique**, and a stored version is never edited: a request's `matrixVersion` names exactly one rule set (decided 28 September, audit R129 (2)). **Never null** (ADAM CR-102, CHG-R10ID-015): the server sets it, 1 for a new matrix and the previous version plus one after; it is not sent and is ignored on input.

ApprovalMode.description:
11.1.43–11.1.46. **Sequential** asks one at a time, **parallel** asks everyone at once, **consensus** needs all of them, **majority** needs more than half.
Parallel and consensus differ in when it completes: parallel completes on the first approval, consensus waits for all. Conflating them is how a four-eyes rule turns into a one-eye rule.

rerouteOnNoApprover.description: BL-154. **An approver on leave is an approval that waits for them to come back.** Reroutes to the next in the chain rather than stalling — `workforce` already knows who is on leave, and an approval queue nobody is watching is the thing that stops a venue.

allowEmailApproval.description: **Approving from an email link with no second factor is the weakest path in the system**, so it is off by default and available only below a configured value.

reopenedFrom.description: **Reopening a decided approval creates a new one that points back.** Editing a decision in place destroys the record of what was originally approved, which is the only thing an audit wants.

attributes.description: **The attributes the raising contract sent** (`CreateApprovalRequest.attributes`), stored as given (ADAM CR-172, fix round 3; CHG-CRA-005). The rules match on them (`matchAttributes`), also when a draft is submitted later, and the contract that applies the decision reads them back with the request (`approvals#requestRecords`): Subscription's `approval.granted` consumer takes a tenant suspension's `action`, mode, reason, `effectiveAt` and notice from here. Null where none were sent.

requestedByPrincipalId.description: The principal who raised the request, or for whom the raising contract raised it. **Null when a guest raised it** (ADAM CR-101, accepted 15 October 2026; CHG-R10ID-016): a guest is a subject, not a principal, so a guest's privacy request (`exportSubjectData`, `deleteGuestAccount`) records `requestedBySubjectId` instead. Exactly one of the two is set.

requestedBySubjectId.description: **The guest who raised the request** (ADAM CR-101; CHG-R10ID-016), set by the server from the guest session; null for a request a principal raised. Segregation of duties holds for it too: no approver decides a request raised for their own subject.

approvers.description: **The approver chain, fixed when the request is routed** (ADAM CR-102, option 1, accepted 15 October 2026; CHG-R10ID-015). One `approvals.request_approver` row per approver per level, written by `createApprovalRequest` (when not a draft) and `submitApprovalRequest` from the matched rule's roles and the delegations in force at that moment (`isDelegate` true for a delegate standing in). The chain is not recomputed at decision time: `decideApprovalRequest` refuses `notInApproverChain` to anyone with no row at the current level, so a role change after routing neither adds nor removes an approver of a request in flight. An escalation (`escalateApprovalRequest`, the SLA job) and a reroute (`rerouteOnNoApprover`) add rows; a returned or information-requested request keeps its chain when resubmitted. Rows are never edited or deleted.

level.description: The level of the chain this approver decides at.

principalId.description: The approver, a principal of the tenant.

isDelegate.description: True when the approver stands in for another through an `ApprovalDelegation` in force at routing.

pendingApprovers.description: The rows of `approvers` at `currentLevel` who have not decided yet, with their names; derived, not stored (CHG-R10ID-015).

decisions.description: Every decision at every level, in order. **Immutable once the request completes** (11.1.56) — an approval is evidence, and amending one is a different fact.

escalations.description:
11.1.48. Who was asked, when, and why it moved up. **Escalation adds an approver rather than replacing one**, so the original stays in the record.

**Stored as `approvals.escalation` rows, one per escalation, in order** (14 October 2026, CHG-CRD-006, ADAM CR-078: the table held only `id` and `request_id`, so `escalateApprovalRequest` wrote nothing the escalation reports could read). Written by `escalateApprovalRequest` (manual, `wasAutomatic` false) and by the SLA job on a breach (`wasAutomatic` true); read by `getApprovalAnalytics` and the SLA and escalation monitors. Append-only: an escalation is never edited.

reason.description: The requester's or approver's reason; for an automatic escalation, the SLA rule that fired.

escalatedByPrincipalId.description: Who escalated it by hand (`escalateApprovalRequest`'s caller); null for an automatic one.

addedApproverPrincipalId.description: The approver the escalation added at `toLevel`; the original approver stays in the chain.

assignedToPrincipalId.description: Who claimed or was assigned the request in a shared queue (`assignApprovalRequest`; DI-723; CHG-CSP-042). Null while it sits in the queue.

assignedToDepartmentId.description: The department queue it was assigned to, where it went to a department rather than a person (CHG-CSP-042).

assignmentNote.description: The note `assignApprovalRequest` was given, kept with the assignment (R8 blocker APPROVALS-TENANCY-C02, CHG-R8MIG-009).

approvalMatrixId.description: The matrix routing chose at submit (with `matrixVersion`), so a decision is checked against the matrix the request was routed by (CHG-R8MIG-009).

ruleId.description: The matrix rule that matched on kind, scope, amount and `attributes` (CHG-R8MIG-009).

cancelReason.description: Why the request was cancelled, as `cancelApprovalRequest` was given it (CHG-R8MIG-009).

aiAssessment.description: **AI context for the reviewer, never an input to the decision** (11.1.73 to 11.1.75; MoM 8 September; 29 September, build pass, group G2). Written by approvals from `ai.scoreApprovalRequest` on submit and on each SLA tick; null where AI is off or has not answered. Shown on the request labelled as AI; orders the inbox only when `sort=aiPriority` is asked for.

escalationSuggestion.description: A suggestion a person may act on through `escalateApprovalRequest`, or the tenant's own SLA policy may; nothing escalates because of it.

signals.description: The signals behind the scores, largest first, as `ai.AiApprovalRequestScore.signals`.

scoreId.description: The `ai.approval_request_score` row it was copied from; `ai.getApprovalRequestScore` gives the full context. Not a foreign key (the score lives in the AI service).

decisionRecordId.description: The ai decision record, for the audit of what the AI said and why.

id.description: **Added 20 August.** The schema reference derives table columns from API response schemas, and a response is not a table — this one returned everything a caller needs and not the row's own identity, so the table had no key and no row could be addressed, updated or deleted. Found by an audit of all 365 tables, not by a reader.

order.description: **First match wins.** Explicit ordering is what makes a matrix reviewable — an unordered set of overlapping rules is one nobody can reason about.

minAmount.description: **Amounts compare in the venue's currency** (the lead, 25 October 2026, r10 round 3, ADAM CR-102; CHG-R10ID-020): a request amount in another currency (a supplier's, a tender's) is converted into the currency of the venue the request is raised at, at that day's FX rate (finance `listFxRates`), before it is compared with `minAmount` and `maxAmount`; a tenant- or region-level matrix's bounds are read in that same venue currency.

maxAmount.description: The upper bound, compared as `minAmount` is (venue currency, the day''s FX rate; CR-102).

riskScoreAbove.description: 11.1.12. **Not matched against the AI risk score** (29 September, build pass, group G2). The AI assessment on a request (`ApprovalRequest.aiAssessment`, from `ai.scoreApprovalRequest`) is context for the reviewer only (MoM 8 September: AI never influences approve or reject), and routing a request to more approvers because of it would be influence. A rule with this set matches only a `riskScore` the requesting contract passes in `attributes` from its own deterministic rules (a payment's rule score, for example). Using the AI score here needs the client to say so.

condition.description:
11.1.13. Evaluated against the attributes the caller supplied (`CreateApprovalRequest.attributes`, stored on the request).

**The condition language: attribute comparisons joined by AND** (ADAM CR-102, option 1, accepted 15 October 2026; the open decision of pull audit R104, settled for r10; CHG-R10ID-015). It lifts the refusal of R8 blocker cause APPROVALS-TENANCY-C06 (CHG-R8SPN-016), which held only until the grammar was decided. A condition is one or more clauses separated by ` AND ` (upper case, single spaces); there is no OR, no NOT and no parentheses (an OR is two rules). A clause is `<attribute> <operator> <value>`:
- `<attribute>` names a key of the request's `attributes`, by name (`[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]{0,63}`; for example `customerType`, `riskScore`, `department`);
- `<operator>` is one of `=`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `in`, `notIn`;
- `<value>` is a single-quoted string (`'vip'`, a quote inside doubled), a number (`-12.5`), `true` or `false`, or, for `in` and `notIn`, a bracketed list of strings or of numbers (`['a', 'b']`, at most 50).
A condition holds when every clause holds. A clause holds only when the attribute is present and of the value's type (string, number or boolean; `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=` take numbers only); an absent or mistyped attribute makes the clause, and so the rule, not match. Strings compare exactly, case included. At most 10 clauses. `setApprovalMatrix` parses a non-null `condition` and refuses one that does not parse with `422 condition-invalid`, storing nothing, so a stored condition always parses. A rule matches when kind, scope, subject type, amount and `matchAttributes` match and then its `condition`, if any, holds.

**How two conditions are compared for `unreachableRule`.** A later rule is unreachable when an earlier rule always matches first: every request that makes the later rule match also makes the earlier one match. For conditions this is decided clause by clause, and only where it can be proved: the earlier rule's condition is null, or each of its clauses is implied by a clause of the later rule on the same attribute (equal clauses; `= v` implies `!= w` for w other than v, `in` a list holding v and `notIn` a list without v; `> a` implies `> b` and `>= b` for a >= b, and likewise for `<`; `in L` implies `in M` when L is within M). A clause not provably implied counts as reachable, so the check never refuses a matrix that could route a request to the later rule.

approverRoleIds.description: Role ids from `identity.listRoles` (`Role.id`), which is where an editor gets the names to show and pick from. This contract stores the ids only.

approverScopeLevel.description: 11.1.39. Which organisational level the approver must sit at.

levels.description: 11.1.3. Multi-level chains ask each level in turn.

slaMinutes.description: 11.1.14. Null means no SLA, which is different from a long one.

expiresAfterMinutes.description: 11.1.53. An unanswered request eventually stops waiting.

subjectTypes.description:
**Which subjects of the kind this rule matches** (decided 2 October 2026, Chinmay; CHG-CSP-028, CHG-CSP-036, CHG-CSP-031): the `CreateApprovalRequest.subjectType` values, for example `topologyPublication` or `whiteLabelPublication` under `configurationChange`. Empty matches every subject of the kind. It is how a venue switches an optional review step on for one kind of act without routing every act of the kind.
**Except subject type `tenant`**: a tenant's own rules never match it, even with `subjectTypes` empty. A platform suspension or reactivation of a tenant is routed only by the platform rule held in the control plane (`ApprovalKind`; lead's ruling on lane H review 3 N-1, 20 October 2026; CHG-R8SPN-015).

signatureMethods.description: **The signature methods this level accepts, where `requiresSignature` is true** (design-notes correction on ADM-344, Block B: "Configuring which stages need a signature is a policy write"; CHG-CSP-045). Values of `ApprovalSignature.method`. Empty accepts any of them. With `requiresSignature` this makes the rule the signature policy: which levels of which kinds need a signature, and how it is given; `signApprovalDecision` refuses a method the level does not accept.

externalProviderId.description: 11.1.65 (29 September). **This level is decided in an external workflow system** (`ApprovalExternalProvider`) rather than by a person in TICVAI. `approverRoleIds` stay required: they are who decides if the provider does not answer in time and its `onTimeout` is `fallBackToRoles`.

code.description: **A stable code for the rule, unique within its matrix** (4 October 2026, CHG-FXC-005; enforced by a unique index on (`matrix_id`, `code`) since ADAM CR-102, CHG-R10ID-015, compared without case). The composite `approveMatrixMultiLevel` upserts a rule by it; `setApprovalMatrix` may leave it null, and two null codes do not collide. A body with two rules of one code is `400 validation`.

minimumApprovals.description: N in N-of-M (CHG-FXC-005). Null means every approver the mode asks.

requiredApproverRoleId.description: A role that must be among the approvals whatever N is (the CFO in an N-of-M group); it is also one of `approverRoleIds` (CHG-FXC-005).

rejectionBehavior.description: What a rejection at this rule does; null is `rejectRequest` (CHG-FXC-005).

minPercentage.description: A percentage threshold (a discount or a margin impact) at or above which the rule applies, beside `minAmount` (CHG-FXC-005).

matchAttributes.description: **The request attributes a rule matches on** (CHG-FXC-005): keys `module`, `product`, `department`, `customerType`, `risk`, `exceptionType`, `legalEntity`, each an exact value the request's attributes must carry. Every key given must match; an absent key matches anything. Evaluated before `condition`.

compositeMode.description: The `approvalMode` the composite screen sent, kept so it reads back what it saved; `mode`, `levels` and `minimumApprovals` are what the engine runs (CHG-FXC-005).

AttendanceAmendment.description: One correction to an attendance record, appended by `amendAttendance` and never updated (decided 28 September, audit R129 (7)).

occurredAtBefore.description: The record's time before this correction.

occurredAtAfter.description: The time this correction set (`correctedAt` on the request).

recordedAt.description: When the server received it. **Both are kept**: a steward clocking in offline at a gate is not late because the sync was.

amendedByPrincipalId.description: Who made the latest amendment. The full history is `amendments` (audit R129 (7)).

amendmentReason.description: The latest amendment's reason. The full history is `amendments` (audit R129 (7)).

originalOccurredAt.description: **The original is never overwritten.** Attendance feeds pay, and a record that can be quietly rewritten is not evidence.

amendments.description: **Every correction, oldest first, one row each** (decided 28 September, audit R129 (7)). A single set of amendment columns holds only the last one, and the second correction to a record would erase the evidence of the first.

exception.description: Computed against the rota. Null where the record matches what was expected.

CapabilityTemplate.description: 3.3.23, BL-110. **A named tick-set — a role, with nothing depending on the name.**

module.description: **The module a per-module preset belongs to** (a contract name, as `listModuleCapabilities`; CHG-CSP-003). Null for a template that spans modules, such as the Cashier starting configuration.

presetLevel.description: **Which of the three per-module presets this is** (decided 2 October 2026, Chinmay; DEC-007; CHG-CSP-003): All, Viewer or Mid-level. Null on a template a tenant saved itself and on a cross-module starting configuration.

isPreset.description: **Seeded by the platform, not saved by the tenant** (CHG-CSP-003). A preset is offered when a role is created and cannot be deleted; a tenant saves its own tick-sets beside them with `setCapabilityTemplate`.

scopePath.description: **The partition key** (ADR-0005). Written by the server at `tenant` scope; ignored if a request sends it.

initialCredential.description: **Stored hashed, never as sent** (14 October 2026, CHG-CRD-001): `createPrincipal` writes one `identity.principal_credential` row with `method: password` and `credentialHash` the PHC string of this value (ADR-0071). Held to `setPasswordPolicy`. Omitted for a principal who will sign in only through the tenant's single sign-on, who then has no local credential until `resetPrincipalCredential` issues one.

mustChangeCredential.description: Stored on the principal (`Principal.mustChangeCredential`, CHG-CRD-001) and returned at `login`; cleared by the principal's first successful `changeOwnCredential`.

homeScopePath.description: The `platform.scope` path the person works from. **Resolved, not kept:** the path is resolved to the `platform.scope` row at it, whose id is `identity.principal.home_scope_id`; the path itself has no column (CHG-R6G-009). Omitted: the caller's own home scope. At or beneath a node where the caller holds `USER_MANAGE`, or `403` (14 October 2026, ADAM CR-077; CHG-IDR-002).

roleIds.description: Roles granted at once. **Each becomes one `identity.delegated_access` row** (ALLOW, at the home scope's path, granted by the caller), as `createDelegatedAccess` writes it and under the same segregation check; the first is the principal's `primaryRoleId` (14 October 2026, ADAM CR-077; CHG-IDR-002).

IdentityAccessReviewCampaign.description: **A periodic access review** (7.1.35, 7.1.56; decided 29 September, build pass, group G2): which grants, reviewed by whom, by when. Its items are `identity.access_review_item`. Lifecycle in `states/access-review-campaign.yaml`.

scopePath.description: **The partition key** (ADR-0005), and what is reviewed: every grant at or below it. Inside the caller's own scope. Operations write it at `venue` scope.

roleIds.description: Only grants of these roles; null reviews every grant in scope.

reviewerMode.description: `lineManager`: each item goes to the holder's manager from their primary work assignment, falling back to the named reviewers where none is found. `named`: the named reviewers share the items.

decidedCount.description: Kept by `decideAccessReviewItem` in the same write, so the campaign list needs no count query.

IdentityAccessReviewItem.description: One grant under review in a campaign, with the finding that pre-filled it and the reviewer's decision (decided 29 September, build pass, group G2). Lifecycle in `states/access-review-item.yaml`.

IdentityPermissionFinding.x-ticvai-persistence: none — computed from grants (roles, delegations, policies) against identity.access_decision and identity.segregation_rule
IdentityPermissionFinding.description: One excessive, missing or conflicting permission (7.1.47; decided 29 September, build pass).

roleId.description: The role that grants it, for excessive and conflicting; the role whose peers hold it, for missing.

conflictingPermission.description: The other half of the pair, for conflicting.

lastUsedAt.description: The last permit that used it; null when never used in the window.

deniedCount.description: For missing, the denials in the window.

peersHoldingPercent.description: For missing, the share of the role's holders at the same scope who hold the permission.

asDraft.description: True when the finding exists only because of the `draftPolicyId` evaluated.

IdentityRoleSuggestion.x-ticvai-persistence: none — computed from workforce.work_assignment peers, identity.delegated_access and identity.access_decision
IdentityRoleSuggestion.description: One role suggested for a person because peers with the same job title and posting hold it (7.1.35, 7.1.56; decided 29 September, build pass, group G2).

scopePath.description: Where the peers hold it, and so where it would be granted.

peerCount.description: Principals with the same job title at the same posting.

peersUsingPercent.description: Of the peers holding it, the share with a permit using one of its permissions in `lookbackDays`.

recommendation.description: `grant` where most peers hold and use it; `review` where they hold it and do not use it; `held` where the person has it already.

evidence.description: What the suggestion rests on, so the person granting can check it.

requiresApproval.description: Whether granting this role raises an approval (a role carrying permission or price authority, ApprovalKind level 2).

Money.description:
**On the wire this is three fields; in the database it is one column.**
24 August. Every column typed `Money` was landing as `jsonb` — 129 of them, including `orders.shift.opening_float`, `inventory.purchase_order.total` and `promotions.voucher.balance`. **`orders.cash_movement.amount` was `numeric(18,4)` because somebody hand-typed that one**, and the inconsistency is what made it visible.
**A jsonb price cannot be summed in SQL.** Every total, variance and reconciliation moves into application code — and a shift variance computed in .NET against a ledger computed in Postgres is two answers to one question. That is F13 month-end and F98 takings-to-ledger, both walked, both assuming the arithmetic is in the database.
**`currency` and `scale` are not stored per row.** ADR-0018 makes them region-scoped and not overridable below, so they resolve from the scope walk — storing AED against nine million rows in a UAE region is nine million copies of a fact that cannot differ. A row that needed its own currency would be a row in the wrong region.
**They stay on the wire** because a client reading a figure should not have to walk a hierarchy to know what it means.

amount.description: Decimal string, never a float. Up to 4 decimal places. **Persisted as `numeric(18,4)`** — the string is a transport choice, so a JavaScript client cannot round a fare in transit.

currency.description: **Resolved from the region, not stored on the row** (ADR-0018). OMR uses 3 decimal places and AED uses 2 — a venue on a different scale from its region is a ledger that cannot consolidate.

scale.description: Resolved from the region alongside `currency`. **A currency other than the venue's or region's trading currency** (a tourist's USD cash at an AED till, `Payment.tenderAmount`; a guest-selected charge currency, `Order.chargeTotal`; a refund in the tender currency) **takes its ISO 4217 minor units**, held as one fixed list in the kernel (`TICVAI.Domain`, beside Money), so every module resolves it the same way and no table, query or migration holds it (ADAM CR-192, option A; Chinmay, 21 October 2026; CHG-R10ORD-018). The venue and region settings keep their own `currency_scale` for the trading currency.

isActive.description: False causes every permission query at or beneath this node to resolve to DENY.

validTo.description: Past this, resolution returns DENY regardless of grants.

primaryRoleId.description: Determines the landing screen when the principal holds several roles and picks one at login.

roles.description: **Read with the principal, never stored on it** (decided 14 October 2026, ADAM CR-077; CHG-IDR-002): one item per role the principal holds through a live grant, an `identity.delegated_access` row with this `principal_id`, a `role_id`, `effect` ALLOW, `revoked_at` null and now inside `valid_from`..`valid_to` (an open end is open), joined to `identity.role` for `code` and `name`. A role granted at several scopes appears once. `isPrimary` is `role.id = principal.primary_role_id`. Ordered by `name` ascending.

mustChangeCredential.description: **The principal must replace their credential before the session is usable** (14 October 2026, CHG-CRD-001, ADAM CR-078; `createPrincipal` took it and nothing stored it). Set by `createPrincipal` (from `CreatePrincipalRequest.mustChangeCredential`, true unless the creator says otherwise) and by `resetPrincipalCredential` (always true: a reset credential is temporary). **Cleared only by a successful `changeOwnCredential`.** `login` returns it in `LoginResponse.mustChangeCredential`, and while it is true the session may call `changeOwnCredential`, `logout` and nothing else.

ssoProviderId.description: **Set when single sign-on provisioned this principal** (`completeSsoAuthorization`, from the tenant's `identity.sso_provider`; 14 October 2026, CHG-CRD-001). Such a principal has **no local password**: no `password` row in `identity.principal_credential`, a `password` `login` is refused 401 `sso-sign-in-required` (the door offers `startSsoAuthorization` instead), and `changeOwnCredential` with `method: password` is refused 409 `credential-managed-by-sso`. A till PIN may still be issued to them by `resetPrincipalCredential` (`method: pin`); until it is, a `pin` sign-in is refused the same way. Null for a principal created with `createPrincipal`.

temporaryCredential.description: Issued to the principal out of band. Must be changed at next sign-in. Stored as the `credentialHash` of the principal's row for `method` (ADR-0071), and `Principal.mustChangeCredential` is set (CHG-CRD-001).

code.description:
**Unique within the tenant** (decided 28 September, audit R108). A seeded role's code is reserved in every tenant. Unique per tenant, not per venue, because a grant names a role anywhere in the tree; `createRole` refuses a duplicate with `409 duplicate-code`.
**Compared case-insensitively** (`common.yaml`, `x-ticvai-unique`; ADAM CR-079, CHG-IDR-003): `ADMIN` and `admin` are one code, and the second is the duplicate. The code is kept as it was typed.

permissions.description:
**A role that grants no permissions is not a role.** `Role` carried a code, a name and two counts until 18 August, and `identity.role_permission` derived from it with exactly one column — `role_id`. **A join table that joins to nothing**, found by Hrushikant in review and missed by the schema audit that ran the same day.
**The audit asked whether every table had columns, a relationship and an owner, and this table had all three.** What it did not ask is whether a table with one column can do the job its name claims.
**The role's own set, not revoked** (decided 14 October 2026, ADAM CR-077; CHG-IDR-002): the `identity.role_permission` rows of this role with `is_active` true. A revoked row is history, not a permission. **Inherited permissions are not merged in**: a client reads `inheritsFromRoleId` and that role, the same shape `setRolePermissions` returns (`permissions` beside `inheritsFromRoleId`). The segregation check is the one place the two are taken together (ADAM CR-079).

inheritsFromRoleId.description:
**Role composition, one level deep and no deeper.** A supervisor role that is a cashier plus three permissions is how venues actually describe them.
**Cycles are refused and depth is capped at one**, because a permission set nobody can read off the screen is a permission set nobody audits.

isSystem.description:
**Seeded roles ship and are editable; deleting one is refused.** A venue that removes `cashier` and rebuilds it has two roles with one name in the audit log.
**The seeded system roles are Cashier, Supervisor, Venue Manager, Finance and Tenant Admin** (proposed in `docs/active/seed-data-proposal.md` section 2, client to correct; audit R229).

**Superseded 2 October 2026: no fixed default roles** (Chinmay; DEC-007; CHG-CSP-003). The five are presets (`CapabilityTemplate`, `isPreset`) a role starts from, not roles a tenant is given. The field stays for clients built at r1 and is false on every role created from 2 October.

presetCode.description: **The preset this role was started from, for the record only** (decided 2 October 2026, Chinmay; DEC-007; CHG-CSP-003): the first of `createRole.presetCodes`, or null for a role ticked by hand. It binds nothing; a later edit of the preset never changes this role.

principalCount.description: **Computed on read, never stored** (decided 14 October 2026, ADAM CR-077; CHG-IDR-002): the distinct principals holding this role through a live grant (`identity.delegated_access` with this `role_id`, a `principal_id`, `effect` ALLOW, `revoked_at` null, now inside its validity window). **Counted under row-level security**, so only the grants the caller's own grants let it read are counted: a venue manager sees the venue's holders, not the tenant's.

grantCount.description: **Computed on read, never stored** (decided 14 October 2026, ADAM CR-077; CHG-IDR-002): the live grants of this role (the rows `principalCount` counts, one per grant, so a principal granted the role at two scopes counts twice). Counted under row-level security, as `principalCount`.

isPrimary.description: True for the role that is the principal's `primaryRoleId` (`identity.principal.primary_role_id`); false for the others (14 October 2026, ADAM CR-077; CHG-IDR-002).

grantId.description: **The grant this card stands for** (`identity.delegated_access.id`; IDENTITY-C45, CHG-R8SPN-032). A role held at two venues is two grants and two cards; `selectRole` takes the chosen one.

scope.description: The scope node the grant is held at (`platform.scope`), with its name, so the card can say which venue (IDENTITY-C45).

overtimeMinutes.description: BL-044, 1.2.83. **UAE labour law limits working hours and mandates rest periods**, and nothing in the package counted either. Derived from attendance against the shift.

restPeriodBefore.description: Minutes since the previous shift ended. **The check that stops a closing shift followed by an opening one**, which is legal in most places and unsafe in all of them.

breachesWorkingHourLimit.description: **Flagged at assignment, not discovered at payroll.** A rota that breaches a statutory limit is a rota somebody has to redo, and finding out a month later means it was worked.

labourCost.description: **Cost at the point of scheduling.** A manager building a rota without seeing its cost is a manager who finds out from finance.

position.description:
What they are rostered to do — gate steward, cashier, lifeguard, technician. **Most positions never touch a till**, which is why a rota assignment is not a shift.
**A position code, not a label.** It is the same value as `StaffingRules.minimumCover[].positionCode`, `OpenShift.positionCode` and `StaffingCoverage.positionCode`: coverage counts rostered people per position, so an assignment spelled differently from the rule it fills is counted against nothing and the gap stays open. Tenant-defined, which is why it is not an enum here.

requiredRoleId.description: Checked on assignment. A rota naming someone unqualified is a rota that gets overridden.

workstationId.description: Where the position needs a till. **The link between a rota and a cash session**, without merging the two.

ScopedPermissions.description: Permissions effective at a given scope path, after deny resolution. Clients filter navigation on this and never compute permissions themselves.

scope.description: Scope nodes this session may act within, resolved once at login from the ltree hierarchy with deny-overrides-allow. Clients filter navigation against this — they never compute it.

effectivePermissions.description: Flattened set across all granted scopes, after deny resolution. Convenience for coarse checks only: it never decides an operation by itself (ADAM CR-189). Anything scope-sensitive uses `permissionsByScope`.

permissionsByScope.description:
Permissions effective at each granted scope path, after deny resolution. Clients filter navigation on this and never compute permissions themselves.

**The server keeps the same set and authorises from it** (decided 25 October 2026, Chinmay, ADAM CR-189 option A; CHG-R10ID-001). The rule for every operation: `x-ticvai-permission` is evaluated at the scope the operation acts on, from the per-scope set (the node acted on or one of its ancestors); `effectivePermissions` is for coarse checks only. A list's reach is the scope paths where its permission holds, and a filter outside it is `403`; a tenant-level operation needs its permission at the tenant root. The request kernel's seam carries this set beside the flat one (#27692 owns the field) and sign-in (#27666) fills it from the same resolution that fills this property; tests fill the seam until sign-in lands. The full statement is `docs/architecture/specs/permission-resolution.md` section 7.2. No wire shape changes.

saleBoardId.description:
Landing surface, derived from the WORKSTATION, not the role (12 Aug 2026 §3). Ticketing, F&B or Retail board.

**Optional since 2 October 2026: only a till session carries it** (Chinmay, door follow-ups; CHG-CSP-002; breaking change against r1 approved as BC-001 to BC-005 in `docs/active/breaking-changes.yaml`). A browser door (ADM-001, SUP-001, PTR-001) and a staff handheld (EMP-001) sign in with no workstation since CHG-DOOR-001, so they have no board to land on and the field is absent. On a till it is the workstation's effective board: the outlet's board unless the till overrides it (`tenancy.Workstation.saleBoardSource`; CHG-CSP-006). A client reads its landing from this field when present and from its own platform otherwise.

availableRoles.description: **The roles the principal may choose, one per grant** (IDENTITY-C45, CHG-R8SPN-032), resolved on read as `LoginResponse.availableRoles` is, so EMP-002 can list them on a cold open or after a relaunch (`getCurrentSession`) without signing in again.

expiresAt.description: When the session ends at the latest: `openedAt` plus `PasswordPolicy.sessionMaxHours` (12 hours by default; proposed, client to correct). A till session ends earlier, when the shift on its workstation closes; any session ends at `logout` or a revocation. Refreshing the access token never moves this time (IDENTITY-C25, FOUNDATION-AI-C27; CHG-R8SPN-014).

SessionStatus.description:
**The life of one signed-in session, which is not the life of a shift.** A shift holds the float and survives a break; a session holds the person and does not. `ShiftStatus.suspended` is where a break lives — *break cover; float intact, workstation released* — and the release of the workstation is exactly why the session ends rather than pausing: the next person opens their own.
**One principal, one active session per workstation.** Enforced by the `ActiveSession` registry rather than by a state, because it is a fact about the set of sessions and not about any one of them.

Shift.description: **`approvals` and `incidents` are child rows** (26 September, pull audit R099): `orders.pos_shift_approval` and `orders.pos_shift_incident`, one row per item, keyed to the shift. Until then the contract carried both and `orders.pos_shift` had nowhere to put either.

id.description: Client-generated UUIDv7. Also the idempotency key.

principalId.description: Who opened it. Cash reconciles to a person and a drawer.

incidents.description:
BL-097. **A till has exceptions and there was nowhere to write them** — a no-sale, a drawer opened without a transaction, a manager override, a guest dispute.
**This is the log a cash-up investigation starts from**, and a shift that balances with four unexplained no-sales is not a shift that balanced.

currency.description:
**Resolved from the region, not stored** (ADR-0018, 24 August). Region-scoped and not overri dable below, so a row in a UAE region is AED and cannot be anything else. **Kept on the wire , removed from the table** — a client should not walk a hierarchy to read a figure, and the  database should not hold nine million copies of AED. Four tables genuinely differ from their
 region and keep a stored currency: `orders.payment.tender_currency`, `inventory.supplier`, 
`ledger.account`, `control.partner_agreement`.

currencyScale.description:
**Resolved from the region, not stored** (ADR-0018, 24 August). Region-scoped and not overri dable below, so a row in a UAE region is AED and cannot be anything else — storing it per ro w is a copy of a fact that cannot differ. **Kept on the wire, removed from the table**: a cl ient reading a figure should not walk a hierarchy to know what it means, and the database sh ould not hold nine million copies of AED. Four tables genuinely differ from their region and
 keep a stored currency — `orders.payment.tender_currency`, `inventory.supplier`, `ledger.ac
count`, `control.partner_agreement`. **A guest paying USD at an AED venue is a real row; a w orkstation with its own currency is a misconfiguration.**

salesTotal.description: What the till took in sales, as the guest paid it — tax included: the shift's takings, not Gross sales (CHG-FIN-002, CHG-FIN-010). **Shown to the shift's own cashier only as one total across every tender** ("Sales this shift" on POS-025; the lead, 3 October 2026, CHG-RONEC-002): with no cash share it cannot be turned into the expected cash, so the blind close holds (CHG-FIN-003). The cash share, the tender split, `expectedCash` and `variance` stay with the supervisor.

refundsTotal.description: What the till paid back, as the guest was refunded it — tax included.

liftsTotal.description: Cash taken out mid-shift by lifts and withdrawals. Cash, so neither gross nor net.

expectedCash.description: 26 September, pull audit R207. **The figure the blind count was measured against**, revealed once the count is in — null until then. Until this date only `ShiftCloseResult` carried it, returned once by `closeShift`, so BO-040 could not show the over/short it exists to accept. **Null to the shift's own cashier on every read** (CHG-FIN-003, 2 October): returned only to a caller holding OVERSHORT_ACCEPT or SHIFT_CLOSE_OTHER at the venue.

countedCash.description: What the close count found. Null until the shift is counted.

variance.description: Counted minus expected, as `ShiftCloseResult.variance`. Negative is short. Null to the shift's own cashier, as `expectedCash` (CHG-FIN-003).

cashierReason.description: What the cashier said went wrong, given with the blind count (`CloseShiftRequest.cashierReason`, DI-803) without seeing the variance; the supervisor reads it beside the variance on BO-040 (CHG-FIN-003).

cashierNote.description: The cashier's note with the count (`CloseShiftRequest.notes`; CHG-FIN-003).

varianceReasonRequired.description: **Computed, not stored** (CHG-R4-019): true while the shift is `pendingClosure` because its count differs from the expected figure within the threshold and no `cashierReason` is recorded. The till shows "Give a reason to close" (POS-007, EMP-009), BO-040 and BO-043 list it as waiting for a reason; `giveShiftVarianceReason` or `approveShiftClose` clears it. Shown to the shift's own cashier, since it carries no figure (CHG-FIN-003).

heldLeaseCount.description: Inventory leases currently held by this workstation. Surfaced so an operator closing a shift can see what will be returned.

businessDate.description: **The business day the shift belongs to** (12 October 2026, CHG-R6-032): the venue-local date of `openedAt` taken against the venue's `businessDayCutoff` (tenancy `VenueSettings`, inheriting the tenant default, default 00:00). Set once when the shift opens and never moved, so a shift opened at 23:00 and closed at 01:00 stays on the day it opened. The daily reconciliation (BO-043) lists the shifts of one business date, and the period close's `noOpenShifts` check reads it (finance).

recordedAt.description: When the device recorded the open. `openedAt` is the server's time.

suspendReason.description: The `reason` given to `suspendShift`. Cleared on resume.

closedByPrincipalId.description: Who submitted the close count. `reopenShift` refuses an approver who is this principal, and until 26 September there was nothing to compare against (pull audit R099).

recountRequestedAt.description: **Set by `rejectShiftVariance`, cleared by the cashier's recount** (decided 2 October 2026, Chinmay; DEC-175; CHG-CSP-013; DI-804). While set, the shift is `pendingVariance` waiting for the cashier rather than the supervisor: the cashier's view says "Recount requested" instead of "Under review".

recountRequestedByPrincipalId.description: The supervisor who sent the count back (CHG-CSP-013).

recountReason.description: The supervisor's reason, shown to the cashier; never an amount (CHG-CSP-013, CHG-FIN-003).

countNumber.description: How many close counts the shift has had: 0 before the first, 1 after it, 2 after a recount (CHG-CSP-013). The latest is the one measured.

syncedAt.description: Null while the shift has unsynced operations.

kind.description: `open` from `approveShiftOpen`, `close` from `approveShiftClose`, `variance` from `acceptShiftVariance`, `reopen` from `reopenShift` (the supervisor who signed it, the time and the `reason`).

SuggestionBasis.description:
**How the answer was reached, and this is the field the whole design exists for.**
A venue must be able to see that today's price suggestion is a margin rule and next quarter's is a trained model — **the same operation, the same screen, a different basis** — and a screen that cannot say which is a screen that asks a manager to trust arithmetic it will not show.
**Swapping a heuristic for a model is a provider change, not a contract change.** That is the point of the abstraction: the frontend, the audit record and the outcome capture all stay exactly as they are.

SupervisorStepUp.description:
**A supervisor signs the act in place, on the device making the call** (decided 28 September, audit R144). Used where the decision is a same-device step-up rather than an approval request: reopening a shift, recounting a stock count, a retail return above the venue threshold, and (proposed by the coordinator, client to confirm) closing a stock transfer short and cancelling a performance.

**The verification rule, the same on every operation that takes it:** the server checks `credential` against `principalId`; that principal must hold the operation's `x-ticvai-permission` at the operation's scope, must be active at that venue, and must not be the person whose act is being reversed where the operation says so. Any failure is a `403` (`supervisor-step-up-refused`) and nothing is written. **No approval request is raised**, and the operation declares `x-ticvai-step-up: pin`.

**Where `principalId` comes from, on every operation that takes this** (decided 20 October 2026, Chinmay, R8 blocker cause GPS-C31, option A; CHG-R8SPN-035). The PIN prompt shows a picker filled by `identity.listStepUpSupervisors` with the operation's permission: the active principals who hold it at the caller's venue, by display name. The supervisor picks their own name and types their PIN; the prompt sends the picked `principalId` (or, where the prompt asks for an employee number instead, `supervisorUsername`). **Nobody signs their own act**: a `principalId` (or resolved `supervisorUsername`) equal to the caller's own principal is refused `403 supervisor-step-up-refused`, even when the caller holds the permission, and the picker leaves the caller out.

principalId.description: The supervisor signing. Recorded against the act. **Exactly one of `principalId` or `supervisorUsername`** is sent (neither, or both, is `400`; not in the schema as a oneOf, so an r1 client still validates).

supervisorUsername.description: **The supervisor's employee number**, which is what the step-up prompt asks for (R8 blocker fix, IDENTITY-C44). The server resolves it to the principal (`identity.principal.username`, within the tenant) before it checks the PIN; an unknown one is refused exactly as a wrong PIN, `403 supervisor-step-up-refused`, so the prompt does not reveal which employee numbers exist. The act is recorded against the resolved principal. Exactly one of this or `principalId`.

credential.description: The supervisor's staff PIN, as they sign in at a till with it. **A PIN, never a password** (audit R123 (7)). Never stored or returned. Exactly the tenant's `PasswordPolicy.pinLength` digits (4, 6 or 8, the tenant's choice; CHG-CRD-002), which the prompt's keypad takes from `WorkstationContext.pinLength`. The operation never reads Identity's tables to check it; it asks Identity's `verifySupervisorStepUp` query (`x-ticvai-read-via`, CHG-CRD-004), and a wrong PIN counts towards `PasswordPolicy.pinLockoutAfterAttempts` as at sign-in.

TrainingRecord.description: **Drafted 4 September.** One person, one course, one outcome. **The field that matters is the expiry** - a lapsed food-safety or first-aid certificate is a person who may not work a station, and a list without it is a list nobody can roster from.

UpdateRotaAssignmentRequest.x-ticvai-persistence: none — request only; a partial update of workforce.rota_assignment
UpdateRotaAssignmentRequest.description: **A partial update of RotaAssignment** (the CR-089 pattern; CHG-SHP-008): `updateRotaAssignment` sends only what changes, and a field left out keeps its stored value. Nothing is required and nothing has a default, so a generated client never resends a value it did not mean to change. The server's own fields (breachesWorkingHourLimit, displayName, id, overtimeMinutes) are not sendable.

restPeriodBefore.description: Minutes since the previous shift ended. **The check that stops a closing shift followed by an opening one**, which is legal in most places and unsafe in all of them.

labourCost.description: **Cost at the point of scheduling.** A manager building a rota without seeing its cost is a manager who finds out from finance.

position.description:
What they are rostered to do — gate steward, cashier, lifeguard, technician. **Most positions never touch a till**, which is why a rota assignment is not a shift.
**A position code, not a label.** It is the same value as `StaffingRules.minimumCover[].positionCode`, `OpenShift.positionCode` and `StaffingCoverage.positionCode`: coverage counts rostered people per position, so an assignment spelled differently from the rule it fills is counted against nothing and the gap stays open. Tenant-defined, which is why it is not an enum here.

requiredRoleId.description: Checked on assignment. A rota naming someone unqualified is a rota that gets overridden.

workstationId.description: Where the position needs a till. **The link between a rota and a cash session**, without merging the two.

WorkforceJobTitle.description: **Taken from the backend workbook, 20 September.** Stores job/designation definitions such as Cashier, Manager, Chef or Technician.

WorkforceWorkAssignment.description: **Taken from the backend workbook, 20 September.** Assigns an employee to a job and operational location/scope for an effective period.

accessPointId.description: Inherited from the workstation, never selected by the operator.

cellName.description: The cell this workstation's region is served from, which is the cell the commerce host answering this request is deployed in (one cell per tenant per region, ADR-0014): the host fills it from its own configuration and reads no table (ADAM CR-096, CHG-RTE-001). A client uses this only for diagnostics and telemetry tagging — never for routing, which the Control Plane resolves.

deploymentProfile.description: Whether this surface reads catalogue locally (ADR-0013). Determines which flows the client enables offline.

pinLength.description: **The tenant's `PasswordPolicy.pinLength`, carried to the device** (14 October 2026, CHG-CRD-002, ADAM CR-078). A device door draws its PIN keypad, and its supervisor step-up prompt, at this many digits; the device keeps it with the workstation context of the last session on it, so the door needs nothing fetched before sign-in. A device that has never had a session accepts 4 to 8 digits and the server decides. Read from `identity.password_policy`, not stored on the workstation.
